problem.title: What happens when the soil loses its balance?
problem.intro: Soil moisture is not an isolated measurement. It links rainfall, vegetation, crops, and the water that seeps deeper. When it changes over time, these systems change with it.

cards.title: Weakened farmland
cards.text: Less water in the top few inches of soil means earlier stress for seedlings and higher irrigation needs. Crop growth depends directly on this reserve.

cards.title: Ecosystems under pressure
cards.text: Vegetation, wetlands, and livestock depend on the water available. A harsher dry season reduces plant cover and watering points.

cards.title: Invisible but essential water
cards.text: Part of the water in the soil seeps down and recharges aquifers. Soil that stays drier for longer can reduce that recharge.
cards.note: Soil moisture describes the upper soil layers. It is not a measurement of groundwater, and Terra Sense shows no groundwater data.

mission.description: Turning observation into understanding: every result shown can be traced back to the dataset it comes from.

capabilities.label: Earth observation data
capabilities.title: Observe the Earth
capabilities.text: The series come from NASA Giovanni, which averages GLDAS Noah (soil) and MODIS (aerosol) products over the area. Years of monthly values make it possible to tell a season from a lasting change.

capabilities.label: Statistical analysis
capabilities.title: Identify trends
capabilities.text: The Mann-Kendall test tells whether a steady change is statistically supported or compatible with chance. The Theil-Sen slope estimates its size. Neither one establishes a cause.

capabilities.label: Assisted exploration
capabilities.title: Understand the results
capabilities.text: The assistant explains a trend, a p-value, or a method from the platform's own calculations. It is an interpretation tool: it names its sources and says what it does not know. SHAP explanations are future work and are not active today.

science.title: Read a trend, not just a value
science.description: A single month says little. A series of months, tested with robust statistics, tells you whether a change is real.

methods.label: Trend test
methods.title: Mann-Kendall
methods.text: Compares every measurement with every later one to tell whether a series rises or falls consistently. Monthly series use the seasonal version. A trend is called significant when p < 0.05. It does not prove a cause.

methods.label: Slope estimate
methods.title: Theil-Sen
methods.text: The median of the slopes between all pairs of measurements. It estimates the speed of change per year or per decade and resists extreme values.

methods.label: Transparency
methods.title: Data traceability
methods.text: Sources, periods, units, and missing months stay visible, so every result can be read with the right amount of caution.

about.title: About Terra Sense
about.intro: Terra Sense is a platform for exploring soil trends, developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge around the Soil Trend Detective concept. Earth observation series exist, but they are hard to read and harder to interpret: Terra Sense shows them on a globe, plots them over time, and tests whether their changes are statistically supported.
about.scopeText: One area today: Yaoundé, drawn with its seven districts. Values are Giovanni monthly means over the 11.4–11.65°E, 3.75–3.98°N box, from {start} to {end}. GLDAS cells (0.25°) and MODIS cells (1°) are larger than the city, so they describe a regional mean. Missing months stay empty; nothing is interpolated or replaced with zero.
about.sourcesText: Not every variable comes from the same product. Each series is tied to its original dataset.

sources.name: NASA Giovanni
sources.detail: Area-averaged monthly time series exported as CSV.

sources.detail: GLDAS_NOAH025_M_2.1 — evaporation, surface runoff, soil temperature 10–40 cm.

about.mkText: A non-parametric test of whether a series has a statistically detectable monotonic trend. Monthly series use the seasonal version or the Hamed and Rao correction for autocorrelation. It does not demonstrate causation.
about.tsText: A robust estimator of the trend slope, built from the slopes between all pairs of observations.
about.shapText: Future work. No predictive model or SHAP explanation is published today.
about.updatedText: The catalog does not provide an update date. Latest published observation: {end}.
about.kindsText: MODIS is a satellite measurement. GLDAS is a model estimate. Trends, slopes, and p-values are derived results computed by the platform. Photographs on this page are illustrations from Pexels, not data.
about.disclaimer: Terra Sense is an independent project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Attributing data to NASA does not imply that NASA endorses the platform.

assistant.title: Terra Sense Assistant
assistant.welcome: Hello! I'm the Terra Sense assistant. I can help you explore environmental trends and understand the methods used.
assistant.empty: Pick a question to get started.
suggestions: How should I interpret a soil moisture trend?
What is the difference between GLDAS and MERRA-2?
How should I interpret a Theil-Sen slope?
assistant.placeholder: Ask about the data or the methods…
assistant.unavailable: The assistant is unavailable: the data service is not responding. Sources and methods remain available in About.
assistant.error: The answer could not be retrieved.
assistant.sourceGemini: Written by Gemini from the platform's calculations
assistant.disclaimer: Answers can be incomplete. Check the figures in the visualization before drawing scientific conclusions.
